question.problem:
The matrix $R$ is given below. Let ${r}_{1}$, ${r}_{2}$,  ${r}_{3}$ and ${r}_{4}$ be the respective columns of $R.$
Determine if 
$B=\text{{}{r}_{1},{r}_{2},{r}_{3}\text{}}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(R).$ 
If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}$, where ${r}_{4}={x}_{1}{r}_{1}+{x}_{2}{r}_{2}+{x}_{3}{r}_{3}.$ 

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 & 1 & -3 \\ 12 & -6 & 6 & -6\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $R$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}R & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 & 1 & -3 \\ 12 & -6 & 6 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 & -6 \\ 12 & -6 & 6 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-12){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & -6 & -6 & -18\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & -6 & -6 & -18\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+6{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st and $2$nd columns. So, a basis of $\text{Col}(R)$ is $\{{r}_{1},{r}_{2}\}.$ 

Therefore, we conclude that $B=\{{r}_{1},{r}_{2},{r}_{3}\}$ is not a basis of $\text{Col}(R).$
